thread:
molly: Heads up — new HF model onboarding hit a weird tokenizer mismatch. Fast tokenizer present (tokenizer.json) but tokenizer_config.json was missing, and chat template mapping ended up ignored. Generated assistants drop the leading system prompt tokens in some cases. :eyes:

alex: Can you paste the minimal repro and error?

molly: Repro steps are short:
1) hf repo -> `transformers` convert with `tokenizers` fast files present
2) run redwood importer: `redwood import-model --from-hf ./model_dir --name prod/test`
3) inference using the chat template shows message truncation (system prompt removed).

Snippet from the model dir:
```
# tokenizer.json exists (fast)
{ "model": {...}, "vocab": {...} }
# but tokenizer_config.json NOT FOUND -> importer logs a warning
```

importer log: `WARN importer: tokenizer_config.json missing, falling back to slow tokenizer heuristics`

sanjeev: That's the root cause we've seen: when tokenizer_config.json isn't present we fall back and the chat template special token mapping (e.g. role tokens) isn't injected. Fast vs slow tokenizers can have different special token ids, so the kv-cache + chat template alignment gets off by one and truncates.

liz: Did evals show any measurable regression?

eval-bot: Quick eval run on our prompt suite (1000 prompts):
- rouge-L relative drop: 4.2%
- mean token-length change: -3 tokens on assistant outputs
- hallucination checks up 1.8%
Summary: quality regression correlated with missing tokenizer_config.json and chat template mismatch. See /evals/1723 for full logs.

molly: I can repro locally with smaller script. Example inference snippet:
```python
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
resp = c.chat(model="new-hf-test", messages=[{"role":"system","content":"You are concise."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the text"}])
print(resp)
# sometimes response omits system-preface, output shorter
```

alex: Workaround idea: generate a minimal tokenizer_config.json during conversion that pins special tokens and maps chat template names -> token ids. e.g.
```json
{
  "bos_token": "<s>",
  "eos_token": "</s>",
  "unk_token": "<unk>",
  "pad_token": "<pad>",
  "additional_special_tokens": ["<|system|>", "<|user|>", "<|assistant|>"]
}
```

sanjeev: Yep. Also need to run `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids()` with the fast tokenizer to capture exact ids and write a tokenmap artifact that onboarding uses to patch chat templates. Failing to do that means the runtime may assume different ids.

molly: I tried a quick manual fix — created tokenizer_config.json with the additional_special_tokens and re-imported. Inference aligns again and evals revert to baseline. Patch diff:
```diff
+ tokenizer_config.json (new)
+ additional_special_tokens mapping -> fixed chat template
```

liz: Can we add a check in the onboarding CI that fails if tokenizer.json exists but tokenizer_config.json is absent, or at least emits a non-silent warning with remediation steps?

alex: Yes. I'll open a quick PR that: (1) makes importer create tokenizer_config.json from tokenizer.json when absent, (2) produces a tokenmap artifact under `artifacts/token_map.json`, and (3) runs a small token-id sanity check against the chat template.

molly: That sounds perfect. Also calling out quantization experiments: when we ran 8-bit quant later, the tokenizer mismatch still produced the same regression — so it's orthogonal to quantization but amplifies downstream quality diffs because prefix tokens get dropped and sequence length changes.

eval-bot: Filed ev/issue-487 for a full regression run across quant/precision profiles.

liz: Assign to alex for importer fix and to molly for adding a unit test to the onboarding harness. I'll add a GH label `tokenizer-onboarding` and link the eval run.

alex: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/398 — adds the generator + tokenmap checks. PTAL.

deploy-bot: prod/importer v0.24.3 -> v0.24.4 candidate created (chore: tokenizer_config autofill). :rocket:

molly: Thanks — after alex's PR + my test, I re-ran the 1000-prompt eval and metrics back to baseline. Leaving notes in the model onboarding checklist to never ship fast-only tokenizer without explicit tokenmap. :white_check_mark:

liz: Nice. Follow-up: can we include a small `onboarding-smoke` step that loads the model into a dry-run runtime and runs 50 canonical prompts to detect token-drop regressions early?

alex: Adding that to the PR checklist.

molly: OK closing the loop here. If anyone sees similar weird truncations, check for missing tokenizer_config.json -> regenerate from fast tokenizer and re-import. :thumbsup:
